title: The Painter's Son and the Serra do Norte: kinship, myth, and a hundred years
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Painter's Studio and the Rabbi's House

stops.name: Brussels, the birth of a French son in Belgium
stops.date_confidence: attested (en.wikipedia; fr.wikipedia)
stops.campa: A son is born to Raymond Lévi-Strauss, portrait painter, and his wife, in Brussels on the twenty-eighth of November. The parents are French and the stay in Belgium is temporary; the family returns to Paris within months. The registered name is Gustave Claude Lévi-Strauss, the compound surname already the family's own and not a later invention of the anthropologist. On both sides the house is assimilated Jewish, painters on one side and rabbis on the other. Belgium will be, for the rest of his hundred years, an accident of paperwork.
suggested_refs: Belgian civil register entry of 28 November 1908 for Gustave Claude Lévi-Strauss

stops.name: Rue Claude-Lorrain, the apartment in Auteuil
stops.date_confidence: attested for the street, reconstructed for the year: en.wikipedia says only that the family lived on a street of the 16th named after Claude Lorrain, so the year is defaulted to just after the birth. Coordinate corrected from the research pool's 48.8637/2.2769, which lies 2.7 km northeast in Passy
stops.campa: The family settles in the quartier d'Auteuil, on a street of the sixteenth arrondissement named for the painter Claude Lorrain. The father keeps his studio in the apartment; the boy grows up among unsold canvases, stretchers, and turpentine. It is a household where a picture is a made object before it is a subject, where the surface is understood to have been worked. Nothing in it announces an anthropologist. The street runs from rue Boileau to rue Michel-Ange, a short walk from the lycée that will take him at ten.
suggested_refs: Rue Claude-Lorrain, Paris 16e, quartier d'Auteuil

stops.name: Synagogue de Versailles, the war years with the rabbi
stops.date_confidence: attested for the refuge (fr.wikipedia, Synagogue de Versailles); no month is given within 1914-1918 and the month is defaulted. Coordinate corrected from the pool's 48.8021/2.1287, off by about 1.1 km
stops.campa: The father is mobilized and the boy and his mother take refuge in Versailles with the maternal grandfather, rabbi of the synagogue on rue Albert Joly. Four years of a pious and rule-bound house: the calendar of observance, the fixed order of the service, the prescribed and the forbidden set out as a system a child can learn by watching. He will not keep the practice. Whether the years also taught him to see ritual as structure is a reading later commentators supply; the record gives the address and the war.
suggested_refs: The synagogue at 10 rue Albert Joly, Versailles

stops.name: Lycée Janson-de-Sailly, the school on rue de la Pompe
stops.date_confidence: attested 1918-1925 (en.wikipedia); month defaulted to the start of the school year. Coordinate corrected from the pool's 48.8663/2.2727, about 550 m too far west
stops.campa: He enters the Lycée Janson-de-Sailly at 106 rue de la Pompe, one of the grand bourgeois schools of Paris, and stays seven years, taking the baccalauréat at about sixteen. No teacher records him as remarkable. The formation that will matter arrives outside the syllabus: Marx read young, Freud read young, and geology, which teaches him that a landscape is the visible outcome of forces that are not visible, and that the way to read it is to look for the fault under the field.
suggested_refs: Lycée Janson-de-Sailly, 106 rue de la Pompe, Paris 16e

stops.name: Lycée Condorcet, one year of khâgne
stops.date_confidence: attested 1925-1926 (en.wikipedia, 'Lycée Condorcet (1925-1926), preparation for École normale supérieure'); the research pool's 1925-1927 is struck and the month is defaulted
stops.campa: He crosses Paris to the Lycée Condorcet on rue du Havre for khâgne, the preparatory track that feeds the École normale supérieure. He stays one year. Whether he sat the entrance examination and failed, or declined to sit it, no source consulted says; the claim that he refused on principle is dropped here for want of any authority. What is certain is that he leaves Condorcet for the Sorbonne, and that he spends his career outside the normalien network that runs French philosophy.
suggested_refs: Lycée Condorcet, 8 rue du Havre, Paris 9e

stops.name: Sorbonne, law, philosophy, and the agrégation
stops.date_confidence: attested: at the Sorbonne from 1926 (en.wikipedia), agrégation de philosophie in 1931 placed third (en.wikipedia; fr.wikipedia). The pool's 1927 start year is corrected and the month is defaulted
stops.campa: Five years at the Sorbonne, law and philosophy together, and in 1931 the agrégation de philosophie, passed third at twenty-two. Third is a strong result and not a brilliant one. He names three teachers he never had: Marx, Freud, geology. Karl Marx stands already on this atlas, and Sigmund Freud, whose Vienna will empty in the year of the second Brazilian expedition. From all three he takes the same instruction, that what lies on the surface is arranged by something underneath it that does not show.
stops.quote: Teaching and research are not to be confused with training for a profession. Their greatness and their misfortune is that they are a refuge or a mission.
stops.quote_source: Tristes Tropiques (1955), trans. John and Doreen Weightman, Ch. 6, 'The Making of an Anthropologist,' p. 55
suggested_refs: The 1931 agrégation de philosophie results, in which he places third

stops.name: Paris, marriage to Dina Dreyfus
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year (fr.wikipedia); month and day are not given and are defaulted
stops.campa: He marries Dina Dreyfus, an ethnologist, in the year after the agrégation. She is not a wife who waits on the quay: within four years she is in the Mato Grosso, and the first Brazilian missions are made by the two of them together. The pin here is the corpus pin for Paris, the one that already carries Antonin Artaud's Left Bank, Max Müller's winter under Burnouf, and Karl Marx's exile. It will carry Lévi-Strauss for sixty of his hundred years, and it is where the announcement of his death will be made.
suggested_refs: Dina Dreyfus, ethnologist, co-worker on the 1935 and 1938 Brazilian missions

stops.name: Lycée Victor-Duruy, Mont-de-Marsan: the first post
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: fr.wikipedia gives two years of teaching in total across Mont-de-Marsan and Laon after the 1931 agrégation, which puts this posting at roughly 1932-1933. The pool's chronology lens gave 1932-1935 and its geography lens gave 1931-1933; the two contradict each other and neither is adopted
stops.campa: His first post sends him to the Landes, to the Lycée Victor-Duruy at Mont-de-Marsan, to teach philosophy to provincial adolescents. This is the ordinary road for a young agrégé with no patron: a year or two in the departments, then a better lycée, then perhaps Paris at forty. He does the work. Nothing in the timetable of the sixth form points toward the Bororo. The whole detour that follows depends on a proposal he has not yet received, from a man he barely knows.
suggested_refs: Lycée Victor-Duruy, Mont-de-Marsan, Landes

stops.name: Laon, the lycée and the offer from Bouglé
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: placed at roughly 1933-1934 inside the two-year teaching block fr.wikipedia describes. The offer from Célestin Bouglé is attested; its date is not given anywhere consulted
stops.campa: Posted next to Picardy and the lycée at Laon, the cathedral on its ridge above the plain, the same round of philosophy classes. Here the letter reaches him. Célestin Bouglé, at the École normale, is recruiting French academics for a university being founded from nothing in São Paulo, and puts his name forward for the chair of sociology. He has no training in ethnography and has never crossed an ocean. He accepts. The two years in the departments end, and the career that exists begins.
suggested_refs: Célestin Bouglé's recruitment of French academics for the new University of São Paulo

stops.name: Port of Marseille, embarkation for Brazil
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: no source consulted names the port or the sailing date of the 1935 crossing. Marseille is the ordinary French Mediterranean departure for South America; the month and day are defaulted
stops.campa: He sails for Brazil with Dina Dreyfus to take up the chair of sociology at the new University of São Paulo. The port is not recorded in anything reachable; Marseille is where the South American lines leave from, so Marseille is where this atlas puts him. Six years later he will board a converted cargo ship at this same water, stripped of his post by racial law, with three hundred and fifty other people trying to get out of France. On this first crossing he is a philosopher with a teaching contract.
suggested_refs: Passenger manifests of the 1935 Marseille to Santos sailings, not consulted for this dossier

stops.name: Porto de Santos, landfall in Brazil
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction from standard 1930s São Paulo shipping routes; no source documents the port of arrival for this voyage, and the month is defaulted
stops.campa: The ship comes in at the coffee port below the escarpment, the ordinary point of entry for transatlantic passengers bound for São Paulo. From the docks the railway climbs the Serra do Mar to the plateau and the city. The continent he steps onto is the one Alexander von Humboldt entered from the Orinoco a hundred and thirty years earlier, and that Che Guevara will cross by road twenty years after. For now it is simply where his salary is paid; the interior is a thousand kilometres inland and he has no plans for it.
suggested_refs: The Santos to São Paulo railway up the Serra do Mar

stops.name: Buenos Aires, the inherited pin on the steamer route
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction only: no document places Lévi-Strauss in Buenos Aires. The coordinate is the corpus pin inherited byte-identical from borges.journey.json and victoria_ocampo.journey.json, and the date is a placeholder inside the 1935 crossing
stops.campa: The Marseille steamers do not stop at Santos. They run on down the coast to Montevideo and the Río de la Plata, and no passenger list consulted here says whether he went with them. The atlas records the possibility and nothing more. On this pin stand Jorge Luis Borges, in the decade he is reducing narrative to a combinatorial rule, and Victoria Ocampo, whose villa at San Isidro receives every European intellectual who lands. Two ports of one circuit, the same years, and no evidence that any of the three ever met.
suggested_refs: The Marseille to Río de la Plata steamer circuit of the 1930s

stops.name: São Paulo, the chair of sociology
stops.date_confidence: attested 1935-1939 (en.wikipedia); the month is defaulted. Coordinate note: this is the city centre, where the new Faculdade de Filosofia in fact sat in 1935, and not the later Cidade Universitária campus at -23.5595, -46.7313
stops.campa: He teaches sociology at the University of São Paulo for four years, one of a wave of French academics imported to staff an institution invented in 1934. The lectures are the job. What matters happens in the university vacations, when he and Dina Dreyfus organize expeditions into the interior of the country. He arrived a philosopher under contract; he will leave with two field seasons behind him and no intention of teaching sociology again. The chair is the accident and the vacations are the work.
suggested_refs: The Faculdade de Filosofia, Ciências e Letras of the new Universidade de São Paulo, founded 1934

stops.name: Cuiabá, the staging town for the first mission
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: consistent with the Tristes Tropiques itinerary but not named for this leg in any source consulted; the month is defaulted
stops.campa: Cuiabá is the last point of colonial infrastructure before the Mato Grosso opens: a river town of warehouses, mule contractors, and the offices of the telegraph service. Here the party assembles animals, salt, beads, and the cheap trade goods that will buy passage and information from people who have no use for francs. Beyond the town the roads become trails and the trails become the responsibility of guides. He is twenty-seven and has read ethnography rather than done any.
suggested_refs: The outfitting of the 1935 Mato Grosso mission at Cuiabá

stops.name: Caduveo country, the painted faces of the Bodoquena
stops.date_confidence: attested for the visit (fr.wikipedia; en.wikipedia, Tristes Tropiques); the coordinate is a regional approximation, no village site being preserved in the secondary record consulted, and the month is defaulted
stops.campa: Among the Caduveo of the Bodoquena he records the facial and body painting: dense, bilateral, hinged on a diagonal that refuses the symmetry the face itself offers. He copies the designs and keeps them. The chapter he will write reads the paintings as a society drawing, on its own skin, a hierarchy it cannot resolve in life, the contradiction between rank and reciprocity worked out in ink because it cannot be worked out in the village. It is the first time he treats an artefact as a sentence rather than an object.
suggested_refs: The Caduveo face-painting designs copied on the 1935 mission, reproduced in Tristes Tropiques

stops.name: Rio Vermelho, the Bororo villages
stops.date_confidence: attested for the visit (fr.wikipedia; en.wikipedia, Tristes Tropiques); the coordinate is a regional approximation within known Bororo territory, no village site being fixed in the sources consulted, and the month is defaulted
stops.campa: The same mission brings him to Bororo villages on the Rio Vermelho, where the huts stand in a circle around the men's house and the circle is cut by an axis that assigns every family to one half or the other. Marriage crosses the line; the two halves exist in order to exchange. He is looking at a diagram of a kinship rule laid out in packed earth and thatch, at full scale, walked through daily by the people it governs. Everything he writes for the next fifty years begins in this village plan.
suggested_refs: The dual clan organization of the Bororo village, plan and men's house

stops.name: Utiariti, the mission on the Rondon line
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction from the geography of the Rondon telegraph line; no source consulted names Utiariti for this expedition, and the month is defaulted
stops.campa: The second expedition follows the old telegraph line Cândido Rondon drove through the Serra do Norte, a strand of wire across a country the state does not otherwise administer. At Utiariti, on the Papagaio, there is a Salesian mission post and the last regular contact with the outside. Beyond it the line runs on through Nambikwara territory to stations manned by men who have not been relieved in years. The expedition provisions here and will not see another store for months.
suggested_refs: The Rondon telegraph line and the Salesian mission at Utiariti, Papagaio river

stops.name: Serra do Norte, the Nambikwara camps
stops.date_confidence: attested for the fieldwork (fr.wikipedia; en.wikipedia, Nambikwara people). Contradiction left open: en.wikipedia dates the expedition 1938 and fr.wikipedia 1938-1939. The month is defaulted. The Derrida reading noted in the campa is reception recorded as such and was not verified against a source this session
stops.campa: Among the Nambikwara he finds bands of twenty or thirty moving through the dry season with almost nothing, and chiefs whose authority rests on generosity and on speaking well, and who can be abandoned by their people at any time. He asks a chief for something and the man takes his pen and draws wavy lines across paper, then reads the lines aloud to his band. The scene goes into the book. Jacques Derrida will spend a long chapter on it, arguing that the ethnographer staged his own idea of writing and then mourned it.
suggested_refs: The 'writing lesson' chapter of Tristes Tropiques and Derrida's reading of it in De la grammatologie, unverified in this dossier

stops.name: The Ji-Paraná, Mundé and Tupi-Kawahib
stops.date_confidence: attested for the peoples reached (fr.wikipedia); the coordinate is regional, in present-day Rondônia, and the month is defaulted
stops.campa: The last leg pushes northwest to Mundé and Tupi-Kawahib villages in what is now Rondônia. The animals die, the party runs short of food, men fall sick, and members of the support crew do not come back. He reaches groups reduced to a handful of survivors, records what he can in a language he cannot speak, and turns for the coast. In the book this is where the expedition stops being research and becomes endurance, and where he understands that what he has been looking at is an ending.
stops.quote: Adventure has no place in the anthropologist's profession; it is merely one of those unavoidable drawbacks, which detract from his effective work through the incidental loss of weeks or months.
stops.quote_source: Tristes Tropiques (1955), trans. John and Doreen Weightman, Ch. 1, p. 17; minor punctuation variants across the transcriptions consulted
suggested_refs: The Mundé and Tupi-Kawahib chapters of Tristes Tropiques

stops.name: Paris, return to a mobilizing country
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year (en.wikipedia; fr.wikipedia); month and day are not given and are defaulted
stops.campa: He comes back to France as the country mobilizes, four years of Brazil behind him and a planned continuation that will never happen. The collections and the notebooks come with him. He has no post, no book, and no standing beyond a doctorate not yet begun. In this same year Sigmund Freud, who left Vienna the summer before, dies in London, and the scattering of European scholars that will carry Lévi-Strauss to New York is already well under way. He has a few months before the call-up.
suggested_refs: The Brazilian collections brought back in 1939, later held at the Musée de l'Homme

segments.name: The Line, the Law, the Ship

stops.name: The Maginot Line, Lorraine sector
stops.date_confidence: attested for the service in 1939-1940 (fr.wikipedia); the sector is not specified in any source consulted and the coordinate is a general position on the Lorraine defensive line. The description of the duty as liaison work is reconstruction. Month defaulted
stops.campa: Mobilized, he is attached to the Maginot Line through the winter of the drôle de guerre: a fortified frontier facing a war that has not started, garrisoned by men with nothing to do. He will describe the posting later with something close to embarrassment. In May the line is bypassed, in June the armistice is signed. He has spent four years among people who could unmake a chief by walking away from him, and he returns to a country whose government can be unmade in six weeks.
suggested_refs: The Lorraine sector of the Maginot Line during the drôle de guerre

stops.name: Lycée Joffre, Montpellier: struck off
stops.date_confidence: attested: fr.wikipedia gives October 1940 for the dismissal under the Vichy racial laws and lists him among the Lycée Joffre's teachers; the day is not given. Coordinate corrected from the pool's 43.6086/3.8734, about 900 m off
stops.campa: Assigned after the armistice to teach at the Lycée Joffre in Montpellier, he is dismissed within months under the Vichy statute barring Jews from public employment. Marc Bloch's name stands beside his on the same school's roll of teachers; Bloch will be shot by the Gestapo in 1944. The dismissal is not the war and not the occupation. It is a piece of French administrative paper, signed by Frenchmen, removing a French agrégé from a French classroom. It is what decides him to leave.
stops.quote: One must be very naive or dishonest to imagine that men choose their beliefs independently of their situation.
stops.quote_source: Tristes Tropiques (1955), trans. John and Doreen Weightman, Ch. 16, p. 148
suggested_refs: The Vichy Statut des Juifs of October 1940 and its application to the teaching corps

stops.name: Marseille, the Capitaine Paul-Lemerle
stops.date_confidence: attested: the sailing of the Capitaine Paul-Lemerle from Marseille in March 1941 with some 350 refugees is documented (en.wikipedia, André Breton), and fr.wikipedia gives March 1941 for his departure; the exact day rests on the standard record of the voyage
stops.campa: He boards a converted cargo ship at Marseille with some three hundred and fifty other passengers, sleeping in the hold, watched by Vichy police and by German observers who treat the sailing as a test of how many people can be let go. André Breton is aboard, and Victor Serge, and Anna Seghers. The rescue network around Varian Fry has done the paperwork; the New School for Social Research has supplied the position that justifies the visa. Six years ago he left this port with a professor's contract in his pocket.
suggested_refs: The Capitaine Paul-Lemerle, Marseille to Martinique, March 1941

stops.name: Camp du Lazaret, Fort-de-France
stops.date_confidence: attested for the internment in April 1941 (en.wikipedia; en.wikipedia, Tristes Tropiques); the day is not given and is defaulted
stops.campa: The ship puts in at Martinique and the refugees are marched to the Lazaret, a former quarantine station across the bay from Fort-de-France, and held there under guard for weeks by a colonial administration loyal to Vichy. Heat, interrogation, forms, delay. In the book he writes the island as a purgatory between a Europe that has expelled him and an America that has not admitted him, and notes that the men guarding him are paid by the same state that struck his name from the register at Montpellier.
suggested_refs: The Camp du Lazaret at Fort-de-France, internment site of the Paul-Lemerle refugees

stops.name: San Juan, questioned by the FBI
stops.date_confidence: attested for the detention and questioning (en.wikipedia); no date within 1941 is given and the month is defaulted
stops.campa: Released from Martinique, he travels on through Puerto Rico, where he is detained and questioned by the FBI as a Jewish refugee of the left arriving from Vichy territory with a trunk of unexplained documents. The documents are field notes on Nambikwara kinship. He is cleared and allowed on to New York. Albert Einstein made this same landing in 1933 quietly and by prior arrangement, unstopped; the difference between the two arrivals is eight years and a reputation.
suggested_refs: FBI screening of European refugee arrivals through Puerto Rico, 1941

stops.name: New School for Social Research, New York
stops.date_confidence: attested for the appointment (en.wikipedia; fr.wikipedia); the month of arrival is not given and is defaulted
stops.campa: He teaches at the New School on West 12th Street, inside the community of European scholars the school has been gathering since 1933 under the name University in Exile. New York in these years holds more of the European academy than most European capitals do. He is thirty-two, unpublished as an anthropologist, and living on a rescued salary. A few doors along the same street another exile institution is forming, and in it he will meet the man who hands him his method.
suggested_refs: The University in Exile at the New School for Social Research

stops.name: 24 West 12th Street, the École libre des hautes études
stops.date_confidence: attested for the 1942 founding, his founding membership, and the address (en.wikipedia; fr.wikipedia, École libre des hautes études). The coordinate is geocoded from the street number and not taken from a source; the month is defaulted. Correction: the research pool wrongly housed the ELHE inside the New School
stops.campa: French and Belgian scholars found a free university in exile at 24 West 12th Street, financed by the Rockefeller Foundation, near the New School but no part of it. Lévi-Strauss is a founding member. Here he meets Roman Jakobson, who has been doing to the sounds of language what nobody has yet done to anything else: treating them not as things but as positions in a system, defined only by their differences from one another. Lévi-Strauss takes the operation whole and turns it on kinship.
suggested_refs: The École libre des hautes études, 24 West 12th Street, New York, founded 1942

stops.name: Washington, cultural counsellor at the embassy
stops.date_confidence: contradiction flagged and not resolved: en.wikipedia gives 1946-1947 for the posting, fr.wikipedia has him returning to the United States in 1945 to take it up, and the research pool's chronology lens gave 1944-1945, which is struck. Month defaulted
stops.campa: He serves as cultural counsellor at the French embassy in Washington, a diplomatic interlude in which the restored Republic employs a man its predecessor struck off. He marries Rose-Marie Ullmo in 1946; their son Laurent is born in 1947. The centre of gravity is still New York and still Jakobson. He is drafting, in these years, a book that reads marriage rules as a system of exchange between groups, and he is drafting it from a diplomatic office on the wrong side of the Potomac.
suggested_refs: French embassy cultural service records, Washington DC, 1945-1947

stops.name: Sorbonne, the two theses
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of the state doctorate on two theses (en.wikipedia) and for the permanent return to France (fr.wikipedia); month and day are not given and are defaulted
stops.campa: He defends at the Sorbonne, submitting two theses in the French manner, the major one on the elementary structures of kinship and the minor on the family and social life of the Nambikwara. Nine years of Brazil, war, exile, and diplomacy convert in an afternoon into a French academic credential. He is thirty-nine and returns to France for good. The doctorate is the door; everything after it he does from inside the institutions that had no place for him in 1940.
suggested_refs: La Vie familiale et sociale des Indiens Nambikwara, the minor thesis of 1948

segments.name: Kinship, the Indus, and Tristes Tropiques

stops.name: Musée de l'Homme, the Elementary Structures
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of both the book and the appointment as sous-directeur (en.wikipedia; fr.wikipedia); month and day are not given and are defaulted. The 1950 École pratique des hautes études directorship is tagged as reconstruction in the research pool
stops.campa: Les Structures élémentaires de la parenté appears, and he becomes sous-directeur of the Musée de l'Homme in the Palais de Chaillot, facing the Eiffel Tower across the river. The book argues that the incest prohibition is not a rule against something but a rule for something: it forces families to give their daughters away and so obliges them to exchange. Kinship is the accounting system of that exchange. It is read at once as a book about marriage and slowly as a book about how any system of signs works.
suggested_refs: Les Structures élémentaires de la parenté, Presses Universitaires de France, 1949

stops.name: Karachi, the UNESCO journey east
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction: no source consulted dates any leg of the South Asian journey, and the research pool gives only c. 1950 from the general chronology of UNESCO missions. Month and day are defaulted
stops.campa: A UNESCO mission takes him to Pakistan, three years independent, with Karachi as its capital and millions of people in it moved there by partition. He is travelling as an anthropologist attached to an international bureaucracy, the same postwar apparatus for which he writes Race et Histoire in 1952, arguing that no civilization holds a monopoly on progress and that the diversity of cultures is the condition of their advance. The last part of Tristes Tropiques comes out of this journey.
suggested_refs: Race et Histoire, UNESCO, 1952

stops.name: Mohenjo-daro, the grid in the Indus
stops.date_confidence: attested that the site is named in Tristes Tropiques Ch. 14 (en.wikipedia); the visit itself and its date are reconstruction and the month is defaulted. The research pool's reading of the passage as an admiring one is inverted and corrected here
stops.campa: At Mohenjo-daro the excavated streets run straight and cross at right angles, the houses standardized, the drains uniform, a city of the third millennium before Christ laid out like a company town. He does not read this as a marvel of early order. He reads it as a warning: the Indus cities prefigure the mass, standardized, industrial civilization the West believes it invented, and what the spade turns up is not the childhood of humanity but a rehearsal of its present. Five thousand years buys no exemption.
stops.quote: The first thing we see as we travel round the world is our own filth, thrown into the face of mankind.
stops.quote_source: Tristes Tropiques (1955), trans. John and Doreen Weightman, Ch. 4, p. 38. The published Weightman text reads 'mankind'; the variant 'humanity' circulates from a secondary biography and is not the translation
suggested_refs: Chapter 14 of Tristes Tropiques, on Mohenjo-daro and Harappa

stops.name: Lahore, the layered fort
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction from the Pakistan content of Tristes Tropiques; no source consulted places him at Lahore on any date, and the month is defaulted
stops.campa: At Lahore the Mughal fort sits on the debris of everything built there before it, empire over empire, each course of masonry quarried from the one beneath. The image belongs to the geology he read at seventeen: strata, unconformities, a landscape that is a record of forces no longer acting. He had already used it on the Amazon, where the peoples he found were remnants of larger societies destroyed before he arrived. Here he uses it on stone. It is the same operation in both places.
stops.quote: Enthusiastic partisans of the idea of progress are in danger of failing to recognize... the immense riches accumulated by the human race.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Tristes Tropiques (1955), Ch. 38, p. 393, per Wikiquote transcription only; the wording may be abridged at the ellipsis and was not cross-checked against a second source
suggested_refs: The Lahore Fort and the Part 4 chapters of Tristes Tropiques

stops.name: Paris, Tristes Tropiques
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year and the publisher, Librairie Plon (en.wikipedia, Tristes Tropiques); month and day are not given and are defaulted
stops.campa: Librairie Plon publishes Tristes Tropiques: Brazilian fieldwork, shipboard misery, Indus ruins, and a sustained argument against the idea that any of it constitutes progress. The book opens by disowning its own genre. He has spent six years writing monographs nobody outside the discipline reads, and within a season he is a public figure in France on the strength of the one book he wrote as literature. John Russell will translate it in 1961 as A World on the Wane, abridged.
stops.quote_source: Tristes Tropiques (1955), trans. John and Doreen Weightman, Ch. 1, p. 17, the book's opening sentence
suggested_refs: Tristes Tropiques, Librairie Plon, 1955; A World on the Wane, trans. John Russell, Hutchinson, 1961; the complete Weightman translation, 1973

stops.name: Collège de France, the chair
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of election (en.wikipedia; fr.wikipedia), for the 1960 founding of the Laboratoire d'anthropologie sociale and for the 1961 founding of L'Homme (fr.wikipedia); month and day are not given and are defaulted
stops.campa: He is elected to a chair of Social Anthropology at the Collège de France, place Marcelin Berthelot, an institution with no students, no examinations, and no degrees, where a professor is required only to lecture in public on what he is currently working out. In 1960 he founds the Laboratoire d'anthropologie sociale there; in 1961 he starts the journal L'Homme with Émile Benveniste and Pierre Gourou. He holds the chair twenty-three years and does all his major work from it.
stops.quote: The scientific mind does not so much provide the right answers as ask the right questions.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to The Raw and the Cooked, 1975 English edition, trans. Doreen and John Weightman, p. 7, per Wikiquote transcription only; widely circulated as an epigram and not verified against the primary text
suggested_refs: The Laboratoire d'anthropologie sociale, Collège de France, founded 1960

stops.name: Paris, La Pensée sauvage
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year (en.wikipedia); month and day are not given and are defaulted
stops.campa: La Pensée sauvage argues that the thought of people without writing is not a lesser version of scientific thought but a different and complete operation on the world, a bricolage that builds with whatever is to hand and classifies exhaustively because classification is the point. The animals of a totemic system are not chosen because they are useful. They are chosen because they can carry differences, and a set of differences is what a society needs in order to think itself.
stops.quote: We can understand, too, that natural species are chosen not because they are 'good to eat' but because they are 'good to think.'
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Totemism (1962), trans. Rodney Needham, p. 89, per Wikiquote transcription only; the bonnes à penser formula is universally repeated in the secondary literature but the page was not verified
suggested_refs: La Pensée sauvage, Plon, 1962, and Le Totémisme aujourd'hui, PUF, 1962

stops.name: Paris, the Mythologiques
stops.date_confidence: attested: the cycle runs from Le Cru et le cuit in 1964 to L'Homme nu in 1971 (fr.wikipedia; en.wikipedia gives the looser 1960s-1971). The date is that of the first volume, with month and day defaulted
stops.campa: Le Cru et le cuit opens a four-volume cycle that takes seven years and ends with L'Homme nu. He begins with one Bororo myth and follows it through hundreds of variants across both Americas, treating each as a transformation of the others, the way a musician treats a theme. Honey and ashes, table manners, the naked man. The English editions appear under the title Introduction to a Science of Mythology. He is arguing that myths think themselves through people, and that the rules are recoverable.
stops.quote: I am not far from believing that, in our own societies, history has replaced mythology.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Myth and Meaning (1978), Ch. 4, per Wikiquote transcription only; single-source attribution, not cross-checked
suggested_refs: Mythologiques: Le Cru et le cuit (1964), Du miel aux cendres (1967), L'Origine des manières de table (1968), L'Homme nu (1971)

stops.name: Institut de France, the fauteuil under the cupola
stops.date_confidence: attested: the Académie française's own register gives the election as 24 May 1973 and the reception under the cupola as 27 June 1974, fauteuil 29, succeeding Henry de Montherlant. English Wikipedia's 14 May 1973 is struck, and the research pool's geography lens conflated election with reception
stops.campa: The Académie française elects him to fauteuil 29, the seat of Henry de Montherlant, on the twenty-fourth of May. He is received under the cupola on the quai de Conti thirteen months later, in the green coat and the sword, and delivers the eulogy of his predecessor. The same year he takes the Erasmus Prize. An institution founded to fix the French language admits a man whose working life was spent recording languages that had no académie and, by the time he reached them, almost no speakers.
suggested_refs: The Académie française register for fauteuil 29: election 24 May 1973, reception 27 June 1974

stops.name: Tokyo, the late journeys
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction only: the repeated Japan visits from the later 1970s into the 1980s and the late book of essays on Japan rest on general biographical knowledge and were not confirmed in any source reached for this dossier. Month and day are defaulted
stops.campa: In his late sixties he begins going to Japan, and keeps going back into the 1980s. The country occupies him enough to produce a late book of essays on its aesthetics and its social forms, the only sustained work he devotes to a literate civilization outside Europe. These are the last real journeys of a life that has otherwise settled into the round between the sixteenth arrondissement, the Collège de France, and a country house in Burgundy. The atlas records them on reconstruction, not on a dated itinerary.
suggested_refs: L'Autre Face de la lune: écrits sur le Japon, collected late essays
sources: research pool, afterlife and geography lenses, both marking this as unconfirmed

stops.name: Collège de France, the last lecture
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of retirement from the chair held since 1959 (en.wikipedia; fr.wikipedia); month and day are not given and are defaulted
stops.campa: He retires from the chair at seventy-three, twenty-three years after taking it. The Laboratoire d'anthropologie sociale continues; he keeps working, publishing on masks, on Japan, on the Amerindian material he has never finished with. He has outlived the vogue his name carried in the 1960s and will outlive its reaction too. The discipline he changed is by now arguing about whether he changed it correctly, which is the only durable form of influence there is. He has twenty-seven years left.
stops.quote: I never had, and still do not have, the perception of feeling my personal identity.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Myth and Meaning (1978), Introduction, per Wikiquote transcription only; single-source attribution, not cross-checked
suggested_refs: La Voie des masques (1975) and the post-retirement essays

stops.name: Paris, the Pléiade
stops.date_confidence: attested for May 2008 (en.wikipedia; fr.wikipedia, which adds that he selected the contents himself); the day is not given and is defaulted
stops.campa: Gallimard publishes Oeuvres in the Bibliothèque de la Pléiade, one volume on India paper, in a collection that is, in France, a form of canonization ordinarily reserved for the dead. He is ninety-nine, one of very few living authors ever admitted, and the selection of texts is made by him. Which of his own books he judged worth keeping, and which he let go, the volume answers in his own hand; this dossier does not reconstruct the table of contents from memory.
suggested_refs: Claude Lévi-Strauss, Oeuvres, Bibliothèque de la Pléiade, Gallimard, May 2008

stops.name: Musée du Quai Branly, the centenary
stops.date_confidence: attested: the hundredth birthday falls on 28 November 2008 and he is the first member of the Académie française to reach it (en.wikipedia); the centenary exhibitions at the Quai Branly and the Bibliothèque nationale and the visit from Nicolas Sarkozy are attested for the year (fr.wikipedia) but not dated to the day
stops.campa: He turns a hundred, the first member of the Académie française ever to do so. France marks it with exhibitions at the Musée du Quai Branly and the Bibliothèque nationale, and Nicolas Sarkozy calls on him at home. The Quai Branly holds the collections the Musée de l'Homme once kept, the museum he ran as sous-directeur in 1949, and in its basement there is an auditorium already carrying his name. The objects he catalogued at forty are two floors below a theatre called after him at ninety-nine.
suggested_refs: The Théâtre Claude Lévi-Strauss, Musée du Quai Branly - Jacques Chirac; naming date not established

stops.name: 2 rue des Marronniers, the death in Passy
stops.date_confidence: attested for the date, the address, the cause, and the four-day delay in the announcement (fr.wikipedia; en.wikipedia). The coordinate reconciles two conflicting values in the research pool, 48.8514/2.2694 from the geography lens and 48.859/2.268 from the afterlife lens, to the street's own location
stops.campa: He dies of a heart attack at his apartment on rue des Marronniers, in Passy, on the thirtieth of October, at a hundred years and eleven months. The family says nothing for four days. The announcement comes on the third of November, by which time he is already being buried. Rue Claude-Lorrain, where the painter's studio was and where the boy grew up, lies about two kilometres south across Auteuil, near enough to walk and far enough to be a different quarter of the same arrondissement.
stops.quote: The image a society evolves of the relationship between the living and the dead is, in the final analysis, an attempt, on the level of religious thought, to conceal, embellish or justify the actual relationships which prevail among the living.
stops.quote_source: Tristes Tropiques (1955), trans. John and Doreen Weightman, Ch. 23, p. 246
suggested_refs: 2 rue des Marronniers, Paris 16e, the last address

stops.name: Lignerolles, the grave in the Côte-d'Or
stops.date_confidence: attested for the date, the village, and the country house called Les Charmettes (fr.wikipedia, Lignerolles (Côte-d'Or)). The coordinate is the commune's, not the cemetery plot, and it corrects the research pool's 47.4667/4.6167, which lies roughly fifty kilometres away near Arnay-le-Duc
stops.campa: He is buried in the cemetery of Lignerolles, a village of a few dozen people in the Côte-d'Or where he kept a country house called Les Charmettes. No state funeral, no Panthéon, no cortege down the quai de Conti. A hundred years that opened with a birth certificate issued in Brussels by accident, ran through the Serra do Norte and the hold of the Capitaine Paul-Lemerle and a chair created for one man, close in a Burgundian churchyard, at the address he chose himself and went to every summer.
stops.quote: Natural man did not precede society, nor is he outside it.
stops.quote_source: Tristes Tropiques (1955), trans. John and Doreen Weightman, Ch. 38, p. 392
suggested_refs: The cemetery of Lignerolles, Côte-d'Or, and the house called Les Charmettes
